wire.note: The receipt kind and version are a consumer wire contract. plan-change and implement-plan read kind 'issue' with version 1; do not change the receipt shape or version without a coordinated consumer update. The schema version advances in metadata.contract_version only.

untrusted_fence.note: The untrusted payload must be copied between these machine-owned markers. The checker removes the fenced span before heading, placeholder, record, and citation parsing, so quoted GitHub content inside the fence is inert. Nothing may appear between the section heading and the begin marker, or between the end marker and the next section.

mode.note: The fetcher declares 'single' for --issue-number fetches and 'index' otherwise.

provenance.note: The mechanism string is opaque to this contract. Concrete membership derivation mechanisms (including any label convention) are owned by scope-issue #209; the checker only requires a non-empty mechanism when completeness is verified and null values when it is unverified.

unverified.cand_rule: existence-only within the snapshot issues array

digest.canonical: json.dumps over all fields except digest, sort_keys, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False, UTF-8 encoded
digest.note: The fetcher writes the digest; the artifact metadata must copy it verbatim; the checker recomputes it from the snapshot file and requires both to agree.

freshness.candidate_rule: every CAND issue must resolve in the snapshot with updated_at not postdating fetched_at
freshness.note: Freshness is derived by the checker from the snapshot; it is never duplicated into authored metadata.

SEL.format: - SEL-n: selected: #<issue> | rationale: <reason> | alternatives: none | alternatives: CAND-n why-not-now: <reason>[, CAND-m why-not-now: <reason>]

F.format: - F-n: `path:line` | anchor: `existing text` | observation: verified local behavior

D.format: - D-n: selected: issue-level decision | because: evidence | rejected: alternative and drawback

C.format: - C-n: protected behavior or constraint | status: preserved|modified|at-risk

pre_selection.blocker_evidence: at least one blocker must cite the epic issue or a declared candidate

narrowing.blocker_evidence: at least one blocker must cite the selected child's issue

sel_alternatives.note: Blocked, in-progress, completed, and superseded candidates already carry their why-not-now in readiness evidence, so alternatives cover only the other ready-frontier candidates.

override_membership.verified: the override issue must be a verified child of the epic
override_membership.unverified: the override issue must exist in the snapshot issues array

single_issue_mode.note: Single-issue mode collapses the frontier to one candidate; readiness, SEL presence, and the terminal status still follow the normal status contract. It is a first-class v2 mode, not a v1 migration.

reference_patterns.issue: #\d+ must exist in the snapshot issues array
reference_patterns.f_record: F-\d+ must match a declared F record

citation_verification.note: CAND-n references are validated in their structured fields only; issue and F references are validated in structured fields and record prose.

steps: normalize CRLF and CR to LF
re-serialize the metadata JSON block with sorted keys and compact separators
normalize EOF to exactly one LF
canonicalization.note: The canonicalizer must be a single shared function so the sealer and the receipt verification can never drift.

may: classify readiness from fetched facts plus agent-authored reconciliation
compare ready candidates against the task
select one child or preserve a non-selection result
reconcile the selected child against local source
seal issue-level outcome, scope, exclusions, constraints, protected behavior, evidence, and decisions
must_not: create, edit, comment on, label, close, reopen, or reorder GitHub issues
decompose one broad ticket into new tickets
plan file edits, implementation order, tests, rollout, or rollback
select a blocked issue merely because it has high value
convert arbitrary related issues into epic children

consumers.name: tools/classification runtime
consumers.note: v1 precedence only; the new non-selection statuses collapse to plan-ready until scope-issue #213 updates the classifier.

migration.note: Contract v2 has no v1-to-v2 artifact migration path: plan-change consumes the v1 wire directly and no reader consumes v1 metadata, so no translator exists. Single-issue snapshots are a first-class v2 mode (see single_issue_mode), not a migration of v1 artifacts.
